findings.summary: The new item (KOL-094) is duplicated in the FEATURES.md file.
findings.scenario: The diff adds a new item (KOL-094) under '## Workqueue Items', but it already exists under '## Proposed'. This duplication can lead to confusion and potential double work.

critique.reason: The new item (KOL-094) is added under '## Workqueue Items' in the diff, while it already exists under '## Proposed' in the context.

findings.summary: OAuth logs the authorization code, PKCE verifier, and every code still outstanding.
findings.scenario: An attacker who gains access to the log can redeem any of the outstanding authorization codes for a workspace-wide write token.

critique.reason: The code logs the whole form body at `:133` which includes the one-time `code` and the `code_verifier`, and at `:148` logs every code still outstanding for every user.

findings.summary: OAuth logs include sensitive information such as redirect_uri and state.
findings.scenario: An attacker who gains access to the log can use the redirect_uri and state information to perform phishing attacks or other malicious activities.

critique.reason: The diff shows that `GET /authorize` (`:44`) and `POST /authorize` (`:99`) print their whole query and body, so `redirect_uri` and `state` land there as well.

findings.scenario: The authCodes Map will continue to grow indefinitely, consuming memory and potentially leading to a denial of service.

critique.reason: authCodes is a Map whose expiresAt is only ever read at redemption, so a code nobody redeems is never removed.
